'''André Anders''' (born 1961) is a German-American experimental [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] physicist and [[Materials science|materials scientist]]. He has been the director of the [[Leibniz Institute of Surface Engineering]] in [[Leipzig]], [[Germany]], since 2017. Previously, 1992-2017, he worked at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]], [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]], [[California]].  He is best known for his work on metal plasmas and thin film deposition by cathodic arcs and high power impulse magnetron sputtering. He was the editor-in-chief of ''[[Journal of Applied Physics]]'' (2014-2024) published by [[American Institute of Physics|AIP Publishing]].

== Early life and education ==
He was born in June 1961 in [[Ballenstedt]], [[East Germany|German Democratic Republic]] (East Germany). Early on he became interested in physics, astronomy, electrical engineering but also in music and history. In 7th grade he built a [[refracting telescope]]. In 1980, he studied Physics at the [[University of Wrocław]], [[Wrocław]], [[Poland]], but only until the summer of 1981 because [[Martial law in Poland|Martial Law was imposed in Poland]] (1981-1983).  He continued his studies at [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt-University]] [[Berlin]], East Germany, in the field of pulsed barrier discharges to obtain his "Diplom-Physiker" degree (1984). While being enrolled at Humboldt University, he was also admitted as a grad student to study plasma physics at the Lomonosov [[Moscow State University|Moskau State University]] (1984-1986) in [[Moscow State University|Moscow]], [[Soviet Union]]. He obtained his PhD degree (Dr. rer. nat.) on pulsed atmospheric plasma jets from Humboldt-University, Berlin, in 1987.

== Career ==

=== Plasma physicist in East Berlin, East Germany (1987-1991) ===
His first position was with the Central Institute of Electron Physics of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|Academy of Sciences]] in (East) Berlin, starting in 1987. After just some months of work, he was drafted to serve as a truck driver in the [[National People's Army]] of East Germany. While serving, he used his limited free time to compile his "Formulary for Plasma Physics", published by [[Akademie Verlag|Akademie-Verlag]] in 1990.<ref>{{Citation |last=Anders |first=André |title=A Formulary for Plasma Physics |date=2022-08-01 |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9783112612323/html?lang=en |access-date=2024-03-21 |publisher=De Gruyter |language=de |doi=10.1515/9783112612323 |isbn=978-3-11-261232-3|url-access=subscription }}</ref> After the return to the academy, he worked on improving the lifetime of electrodes in [[Sodium-vapor lamp|high pressure sodium arc lamps]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Anders |first1=A. |last2=Jüttner |first2=B. |date=1990 |title=Cathode mode transition in high-pressure discharge lamps at start-up |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/096032719002200206 |journal=Lighting Research & Technology |language=en |volume=22 |issue=2 |pages=111–115 |doi=10.1177/096032719002200206 |issn=0024-3426|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and developed a laser-based technique to study cathode spots with nanosecond resolution.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anders |first=A. |date=1992 |title=Pulsed dye laser diagnostics of vacuum arc cathode spots |journal=IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science |volume=20 |issue=4 |pages=466–472 |doi=10.1109/27.256775|bibcode=1992ITPS...20..466A }}</ref>

=== Plasma applications in Berkeley, California (1992-2017) ===
As Staff Scientist and since 2001 Group Leader, he worked in various fields of ion beam and plasma applications, including [[Plasma-immersion ion implantation|plasma immersion ion implantation and deposition]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Handbook of Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation and Deposition {{!}} Wiley |url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Handbook+of+Plasma+Immersion+Ion+Implantation+and+Deposition-p-9780471246985 |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=Wiley.com |language=en-us}}</ref> and plasma diagnostics of vacuum arcs.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anders |first=André |date=1997-01-01 |title=Ion charge state distributions of vacuum arc plasmas: The origin of species |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.55.969 |journal=Physical Review E |volume=55 |issue=1 |pages=969–981 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.55.969|bibcode=1997PhRvE..55..969A |url-access=subscription }}</ref> His text book on cathodic arcs<ref>{{cite book |title=Cathodic Arcs |url=http://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-79108-1/  |series=Springer Series on Atomic, Optical, and Plasma Physics |date=2008 |volume=50 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-0-387-79108-1|isbn=978-0-387-79107-4 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and his generalized structure zone diagram<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anders |first=André |date=2010 |title=A structure zone diagram including plasma-based deposition and ion etching |journal=Thin Solid Films |volume=518 |issue=15 |pages=4087–4090 |doi=10.1016/j.tsf.2009.10.145 |bibcode=2010TSF...518.4087A |issn=0040-6090}}</ref> are highly cited.  His work on ultrathin [[diamond-like carbon]] films in the development of [[hard disk drive]]s with storage exceeding 1 GB/in<sup>2</sup> was recognized with an R&D100 Award in 2009.  For more than a decade, he studied the plasma of HiPIMS ([[High-power impulse magnetron sputtering|high power magnetron sputtering]]), especially the role of ionization zones<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Anders |first1=André |last2=Ni |first2=Pavel |last3=Rauch |first3=Albert |date=2012 |title=Drifting localization of ionization runaway: Unraveling the nature of anomalous transport in high power impulse magnetron sputtering |journal=Journal of Applied Physics |volume=111 |issue=5 |pages=053304–053304–13 |doi=10.1063/1.3692978 |bibcode=2012JAP...111e3304A |issn=0021-8979|doi-access=free }}</ref> ("spokes"), self-sputtering<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Andersson |first1=Joakim |last2=Anders |first2=André |date=2009-01-27 |title=Self-Sputtering Far above the Runaway Threshold: An Extraordinary Metal-Ion Generator |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.045003 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=102 |issue=4 |article-number=045003 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.102.045003|pmid=19257430 |bibcode=2009PhRvL.102d5003A |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and gas recycling.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Anders |first1=A |last2=Čapek |first2=J |last3=Hála |first3=M |last4=Martinu |first4=L |date=2011-12-12 |title=The 'recycling trap': a generalized explanation of discharge runaway in high-power impulse magnetron sputtering |journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics |volume=45 |issue=1 |article-number=012003 |doi=10.1088/0022-3727/45/1/012003 |issn=0022-3727}}</ref>

=== Professor of Applied Physics and Director of Leibniz IOM, Leipzig, Germany (since 2017) ===
In 2017, he assumed a joint appointment as full professor of applied physics at the Felix Bloch Institute of Solid State Physics at [[Leipzig University]] and director and CEO ("Vorstand") of the [[Leibniz Institute of Surface Engineering]], both in Leipzig, Germany.

== Editorial work ==
Anders was the editor-in-chief of ''[[Journal of Applied Physics]]'' (2014-2024). Previously was an associate editor of that journal (2009-2014) and served on the editorial boards of ''[[Applied Physics Letters|Applied Physis Letters]]'' and the journal ''Surface and Coatings Technology''.

== Awards and honors ==
*1994: Paul A. Chatterton Young Investigator Award ([https://www.isdeiv.events/home ISDEIV-IEEE])
*1997: [https://www.rd100awards.com/about/ R&D 100 Award] for the Development of the Constricted Plasma Source
*1998: elected Fellow of the [https://www.iop.org/ Institute of Physics (IoP)], UK
*2000: elected Fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|Institute of Electrical and Electronic Engineers (IEEE)]]
*2008: elected Fellow of the [https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm American Physical Society (APS)]
*2009: [https://www.rd100awards.com/about/ R&D 100 Award] for a Pulsed Filtered Arc Deposition System
*2010: Merit Award of [https://ieee-npss.org/ IEEE, Nuclear and Plasma Science Societies]
*2011: Mentor Award of the [https://www.svc.org/awards/svc-fellow-mentor-award/ Society of Vacuum Coaters]
*2011: elected Fellow of the [https://avs.org/awards/society-honors/fellow-of-the-society/ American Vacuum Society (AVS)]
*2014: Walter P. Dyke Award, the highest award of the International Symposia of Discharges and Electrical Insulation ([https://www.isdeiv.events/home ISDEIV-IEEE])
*2016: Nathaniel Sugerman Memorial Award, the highest award of the [https://www.svc.org/awards/nathaniel-sugerman-memorial-award/ Society of Vacuum Coaters]
*2021: R.F. Bunshah Award, the highest award of the [http://www.avs-ased.org/wp/ Advanced Surface Engineering Division] at the AVS
*2024: Leading Scientist Award, The European Joint Committee on Plasma and Ion Surface Engineering

== Books & publications ==
He is an author on over 350 publications, which have been cited more than 23,000 times by other scholars.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Anders |url=https://scholar.google.de/citations?user=PzLUmooAAAAJ&hl=de&oi=ao |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=scholar.google.de}}</ref>

*A. Anders, A Formulary for Plasma Physics. Berlin: Akademie-Verlag, 1990. {{ISBN|3-05-501263-1}} ([https://www.academia.edu/17386711/A_formulary_for_plasma_physics Online]).
*A. Anders, Ed. Handbook of Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation and Deposition. New York: Wiley, 2000. {{ISBN|978-0-471-24698-5}} ([https://www.wiley-vch.de/de/fachgebiete/ingenieurwesen/handbook-of-plasma-immersion-ion-implantation-and-deposition-978-0-471-24698-5 Print]).
*A. Anders, Cathodic Arcs: From Fractal Spots to Energetic Condensation. New York: Springer, 2008. {{ISBN|978-0-387-79107-4}} (Print) and {{ISBN|978-0-387-79108-1}} ([https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-79108-1 Online]).

== Personal life ==
In 1997, he married Christine Kurata, who works in the software industry. They have two children, Mieko and George.  He has also a son, Mark, from a previous marriage.
